app_name: ADHD Habit Tracker, To Do List
title: Not for adhd
body:
As far as apps go, this has good features. However, it is not designed for an ADHD brain, so it really shouldn’t be in the actual name of the app.

This would be useful for people wanting to build habits and track progress … but if you have an ADHD brain this would work no better than any other journal / planner. I have a bunch of them. They are usually good for a couple of days before I forget about them. I knew within minutes of getting this app that it would be another one of those.

On top of that, when I went to cancel the free trial, it didn’t have the amount of $6-7 monthly (and “50% off!”) as it did when I clicked ok - It was going to be billing me the $79 for the full year! To me, this seems like a trap to get people with adhd to download it and then get billed for the whole year!! Because if I hadn’t known so quickly it wouldn’t work, and if I hadn’t been free from distractions in that moment, I 100% would have forgotten, and there goes my food budget for the next week. ADHD tax would have struck again.

app_name: ADHD Habit Tracker, To Do List
title: Too chaotic
body:
I want to like this app, but it doesn’t permit me to change the order of my list of habits at all, according to either chronology or priority, which makes it unusable. I will never maintain a habit I’m supposed to do in the morning if I can’t see it at the top of my list, for example. Not to mention viewing the jumble of random habits in a random order instantly makes me overwhelmed. Maybe if there was any ordering structure at all, or filters. But it’s not chronological, alphabetical, based on color or based on task type. Is it just the list of habits in the order I created them? *screams in disorganization*

Less critically, I’d also like to be able to change my habit type after creating the habit. Say I was tracking time spent stretching but using the timer was too fussy/I don’t always want my phone near me for that, so I decide I just want to check off a box instead. I have to delete my habit, lose my completion stats, and start a new one. It’s just a bit clunky. Having to delete/lose stats is demotivating.

My stat page should reflect the things I'm actually doing and collecting. This seems so obvious to me I feel stupid paying for this app for "lifetime". Example. I have 2 categories "Quality time with spouse" and "alone time". I want to track what that looks like over 14 days and depending on results THEN I might set goals. app_name: ADHD Habit Tracker, To Do List
title: Deleted my other Habit tracker apps
body:
There are a surprising number of ways this app can be used. Aside from checking activities off your list, you can classify habits under “Goal” or “Limit”. That got me considering the things I should be cutting down on (like coffee intake), in addition to what I’d like to incorporate. 

What might be the most interesting aspect is the “Time Tracker” option. For instance, if your “Goal” is exercising 4 hours a week, a stopwatch (under that activity) will be set for that amount. You then start & stop the timer with each workout. No need to guess how long your session was or open a separate app to time yourself. The timer will even continue if you go over the goal amount. The same thing applies if you want to “Limit” time spent on something (like social media use). 

Since I just started using the app, I have yet to see if the Time Tracker is cumulative. It would be cool to see how much time was spent on something indefinitely. 

As I said in the title, I deleted all the other Habit Tracker apps I had on my phone after playing around with this one. For some reason this app just seems more motivating.

title: ADHD Friendly
body:
Having ADHD is not a constant and for everybody the experience is different. But there are some unifying elements that I think most people who suffer from ADHD can agree upon and that is time managment and not only making goals for yourself but actually remembering both to attend to them and that you set them in the first place.

This is where timecap becomes extremely useful, it wont solve the problem but it will definitely help. It keeps me focused and on track. It's like a butler just making sure I remember what those goals were, and doesn't reprimand me if I fail or forget. 

I would like a bit more dicipline from it though since it doesn't seem to notify me when I'm forgetting, but that might be a failure on my part and not knowing how to make it do exactly that. It's only an app and not my own personal Alfred.

I'd recommend it though to anyone that wants to get a better overview of how they want to spend their time and especially if you are like me, have trouble sticking to your goals and/or remembering them. I'd like to add that I'm using the premium version but I'm also all for paying for stuff that works.

It won't transform your life but it can 100% help, if you use it correctly. Either way the responsability always ends with you.

The only thing I wish to be put in would be easier to set reminders for Check Off Activities. Perhaps when we go to edit them there could be an option (there are days you can choose but no times). Would love custom reminders as some goals I’d like to be completed earlier than others (e.g. flossing teeth @9pm vs making bed @8am). The reminders ARE a feature, but are difficult to find (have to click the habit to see the individual tracking page), so it took me a while when I first got the app to find it. 

Thank you!

3. I also don’t really “get” the Timeline tab. It mostly seems to involve a lot of scrolling to see when you did something, which I think could be served better by a vertical layout calendar that’s accessible from that Activity calendar.  
4. I’ve also noticed that I’m sent notifications to finish tasks at my specified notification time even if that task has already been completed, which seems a bit redundant. 

Those are my main notes, and I’m excited to see what comes next. Thanks to the developers for making a cool app. :)

And it reminds me at a certain time (I have my reminder at 9 pm) if my goals haven’t been met. Which is great for somebody like me who tends to forget what I wanted to do. It’s a nice way to gently remind myself of what needs to be done, and to keep track of the times I did them. So when I go back and say “well I haven’t done anything productive....” I can open the app and actually see what daily goals I’ve done, when I did them, and if I spent more or less time doing them every day!!! Honestly- this app is such a simple tool that’s helping me get my life together. The creator/s did such a wonderful job with this.
